findings.description: Task 3.2 / design F4 prescribe the zero-open validate-feature row as `✓ Choices: <n> entries, 0 needs-user`, and say the hook distinguishes ○ vs ✓ only by testing for `choices.json` then calling `needs_user.py`. That reader returns only `needs-user` entries (or silence), so it cannot supply total entry count `n`. Neither 3.0, 3.2, nor F3 specifies another way to obtain `n` (extend the reader, inline JSON length, or drop the count from the row). As written, the documented ✓ form is not producible from the tools the task names.
findings.resolution: Either (a) drop `<n> entries` from the ✓ form (e.g. `✓ Choices: 0 needs-user`), (b) extend `needs_user.py` with a status/count mode both gates use, or (c) explicitly instruct the validate-feature hook to read `len(entries)` from `choices.json` via a skill-relative one-liner. Update F3/F4, 3.0, 3.2, and 3.7 together.

findings.description: Proposal, design F1, and task 3.2 all require echoing the ⚠ Choices form under validate-feature's After Validation prompt when any `needs-user` entry is open. Task 3.7 pins the Choices row in the Step 11 sketch and Step 12 heredoc, and the ○/✓ empty forms, but never asserts After Validation. A SKILL.md rewrite could drop that echo and still pass every 3.7 check while losing the second half of F1's named human decision point.
findings.resolution: Extend task 3.7's validate-feature assertions to require the After Validation section to mention the ⚠ Choices / needs-user echo path that task 3.2 already mandates.

findings.description: F2 and task 3.1 say Step 11.5 compares the fresh ledger's `entries` array and `schema_version` against `git show HEAD:.../choices.json`, ignoring `generated_at`, `run_id`, `git_sha`, `generator`, `event_kind`, `audited_range`, and `auditor`. In the shipped ledger document (`choices_ledger.build_document` / decision-choices schema), `schema_version`, `generated_at`, `run_id`, `git_sha`, `generator`, and `event_kind` live under `header`, not at the document root; `audited_range` and `auditor` are siblings of `entries`. The comparison contract never says `header.schema_version` or that other header fields are ignored as a group, so an implementer can look for a missing top-level `schema_version`, compare the whole `header` (always dirty), or skip the schema bump guard.
findings.resolution: Rewrite F2 and task 3.1 to compare exactly `entries` and `header.schema_version` (parsed JSON equality), and to ignore every other top-level and header field by name. Have 3.7 assert that `header.schema_version` wording, not a bare `schema_version`.

findings.description: Task 3.6 lists skill-workflow.9 and .10 among its covered scenarios via `needs_user.py` reader output. Those scenarios' WHEN clauses are gate presentation in validate-feature and cleanup-feature (`stable_id`/confidence/headline at the human decision point, approve/archive semantics unchanged). The 3.6 assertions only drive the driver and call the reader in a tmp fixture; they never exercise either SKILL.md gate. This is the same overclaim class round 2 already removed for skill-workflow.2, still present for 9–10.
findings.resolution: Narrow 3.6's scenario list to skill-workflow.1, .3–.7, and the reader half of .11 (and optionally reader filtering shared by 9–10 without citing 9–10 as covered). Keep gate-side 9–11 coverage on 3.2/3.3 + 3.7 only.

findings.description: Task 3.0 requires absent ledger → empty stdout for the reader, and separately `--format json` → the same entries as a JSON array. For `--format json` with an absent or unreadable ledger, empty stdout is not a JSON array, while printing `[]` would match the json-mode contract and F3's 'caller can pipe it without branching' intent. The task leaves the json empty-case under-specified relative to text mode.
findings.resolution: Spell the empty cases per format: text → empty stdout; json → `[]`, still exit 0 (and keep the stderr warning on unreadable input).
